name: Balinese Masks Leave-One-Domain-Out (LODO) benchmark
description: Balinese masks are rich cultural artifacts with diverse forms shaped by regional and artistic variations. While prior research on Balinese mask classification has focused on standard supervised learning using a limited public dataset, this study initiates a Leave-One-Domain-Out (LODO) evaluation to better reflect real-world generalization challenges. We enhance the dataset by introducing three new domain variations for each mask class, enabling robust domain generalization experiments. Twelve pretrained deep learning architectures were evaluated using two hyperparameter configurations. Results show that EfficientNet-B0, MobileNetV3-Large, and ResNet101 achieved the highest stability across domains, with weighted F1-score ranges of 0.47, 0.52, and 0.60, respectively. Conversely, Bujuh, Penasar, and Sidakarya were identified as the most challenging classes, exhibiting performance variation ranges of 0.72, 0.42, and 0.57. Hyperparameter tuning, although previously effective, showed minimal benefit under domain shift, with a maximum performance gap of only 14%. This study highlights the necessity of domain-aware evaluation and contributes a new benchmark for cultural heritage classification under domain shift conditions. Future work includes releasing the dataset publicly and exploring advanced domain generalization techniques.
reputation: New, narrowly scoped benchmark introduced by this study with limited adoption so far; of interest to cultural-heritage and domain-generalization researchers.
notes: Small, specialized (cultural heritage) visual dataset with strong domain shift and class imbalance; dataset was not publicly released at time of study; non-LLM vision benchmark.
